spans.s:
Tiṣya occurs twice in the Rigveda, apparently as the name of a star, though Sāyaṇa takes it to mean the sun. It is doubtless identical with the Avestan Tistrya. Later it is the name of a lunar mansion: see nakṣatra.
Foot notes v. 54, 13; x. 64, 8 (with kṛśānu as in archer).
Weber, Naxatra, 2, 290; Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 355; Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East, 32, 331; Keith, śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, 77, n. 1.

6. Tiṣya or puṣya includes the somewhat faint group in the body of the Crab, , and Cancri. The singular is rather curious, as primarily one star would seem to have been meant. and none of the group is at all prominent.
Foot notes Whitney, op. cit., 403, n. 1.

Tisṛ-dhanva, ‘a bow with three (arrows),’ is mentioned as a gift to the priest at the sacrifice in the taittirīya Saṃhitā and in the Brāhmaṇas.
Foot notes i. 8, 19, 1.
taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 3, 4; ii. 7, 9, 2; Satapatha brāhmaṇa, xi. 1, 5, 10; xiv. 1, 1, 7.
